content.jointProblem: Can an uncertainty-aware workflow linking farm policies to verified parcels or buildings and weather grids identify hail-related underpricing more reliably than municipality-level rating? A first pilot would test location matching on independently verified properties, establish whether the available weather data support field-level differentiation, and compare predictive performance against the municipal baseline on held-out storms or years.

rationale.text: Đorđević has directly relevant experience harmonising cadastral parcel identifiers, attributes and geometries, supporting investigation of policy-to-property matching.

sources.quote: Attribute alignment covered parcel identifier structures, tenure type classifications, and area measurement methods.
Katarina Đorđević led the work package on data quality assessment and transformation infrastructure, supervising two research staff and one PhD student

rationale.text: Her regional coordinate-transformation work offers a basis for checking and aligning spatial layers before joining policies, claims and weather data.

sources.quote: This paper derives a locally refined NTv2-compatible grid shift model for the Bačka and Srem subregions using 412 geodetic points
Grid shift files in NTv2 format are provided and tested for direct import into PROJ, QGIS, and FME.

rationale.text: She has demonstrated automated spatial quality-checking methods using tools relevant to a reproducible geospatial pipeline.

executed within a PostGIS environment extended with custom PL/pgSQL functions.

rationale.text: Her evaluation of Vojvodina building footprints is relevant to assessing supplementary location sources without treating their coverage or accuracy as assured.

sources.quote: Completeness ranged from 41% to 78% across municipalities, positional RMSE from 1.1 m to 2.6 m
The framework is designed to be reusable and operationalised as a semi-automated QGIS model.

constraints.text: The workflow must explicitly handle settlement-only policy locations and the daily five-kilometre weather grid; field-level hail intensity cannot be assumed from these inputs alone.

sources.quote: daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: Validation must respect the limited historical sample and distinguish geo-tagged losses from the unresolved locations of the wider insured exposure.

constraints.text: The deliverable must include an agreed automated handoff into pricing, rather than only GIS maps, compatible with the company's Python batch refresh process.

Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh

constraints.text: Company implementation effort must be explicitly allocated within shared pricing and IT teams; a dedicated research unit is unavailable.

sources.quote: The company has no dedicated research unit
a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: Start with a bounded joint-project pilot and confirm supervision and delivery capacity; the researcher reports limited capacity for large commitments before mid-2026.

sources.quote: limited availability for large new commitments before mid-2026
shorter consulting engagements or clearly scoped contract research are more feasible in the near term.

risks: Parcel harmonisation, CRS checking and building-footprint validation have not been demonstrated here for insurance address matching or hail-intensity estimation. The first pilot must test these transfers against independently verified locations and suitable hail observations.
Daily five-kilometre weather data may not resolve narrow hail tracks, even after policy locations are improved; finer-resolution observations or meteorological expertise may be necessary.
The supplied material does not establish hail-modelling or actuarial-pricing expertise. Spatial integration alone may not explain the reported 18% excess claim cost.
Three claim years may contain too few independent storms for stable conclusions; coverage, insured values, repair inflation and claims practices could confound apparent geographic underpricing.
Current researcher availability, budget, delivery dates, data permissions and access to cadastral or finer-resolution weather data remain unknown.
Operational integration could stall: the company's earlier flood-mapping prototype was completed but has not been integrated into pricing.
questions: What are Đorđević's current availability, proposed scope, staffing and budget for a bounded joint-project pilot?
Can the company provide the full insured portfolio, including non-claiming policies, insured values, coverage terms, premiums, exposure dates and event-linked claims—not only geo-tagged losses?
Do policy records contain parcel identifiers, building identifiers or other address evidence, and can an independently verified sample of insured locations be assembled for the first experiment?

What exactly does MeteoVoj supply: hail observations, hail proxies or model estimates? Are event timestamps, uncertainty metadata and independent radar or ground observations available to test field-level differentiation?
Who will provide hail-science and actuarial validation, and what held-out storm or year evaluation and acceptance criteria will be agreed before examining results?
What permissions and privacy safeguards govern policy geolocation, cadastral access and weather-data reuse, and what are the costs of additional data?
Who owns production integration and maintenance, what output contract is required by the pricing pipeline, and how should ambiguous locations and uncertain exposure estimates be handled?
